title: Hull sign German forward Ansah from Union Berlin
description: Hull City sign forward Ilyas Ansah on a five-year deal from Bundesliga side Union Berlin.
fullText:
Hull City have signed forward Ilyas Ansah on a five-year deal from Bundesliga side Union Berlin.

The Germany Under-21 international joins the Tigers for a reported fee of 15m euros (£12.8m) with 12m euros (£10.2m) in add-ons.

He becomes Hull's 13th signing of the summer, with the club having won their first two matches since returning to the Premier League after a nine-year absence.

"I'm very excited. It's a dream come true for me to play in the Premier League, and for such a big club – it's really an honour for me," Ansah said.

"I have heard a lot about the club, the players and the team, and I'm excited to play with the boys and to get to know them.

"I'm definitely a player who always gives his best and leaves it all on the pitch."

The 6ft 4in forward, who turns 22 in November, scored five goals in 36 matches in all competitions for Union Berlin last term.

Hull also look set to sign Tim Iroegbunam after agreeing a £22m package for the Everton midfielder.

title: “Stay Out Of That” – Aaron Judge Goes Off On Red Sox Broadcaster After Incendiary Comments About Jazz Chisholm Jr. & Austin Wells
description: Will Flemming, the Red Sox play-by-play announcer for WEEI radio, faced considerable scrutiny from Yankees fans for his comments during Sunday’s series finale. Among those criticizing him were Yankees captain Aaron Judge.
fullText:
Will Flemming, the Red Sox play-by-play announcer for WEEI radio, faced considerable scrutiny from Yankees fans for his comments during Sunday's series finale. Among those criticizing him were Yankees captain Aaron Judge.

Flemming reportedly made provocative comments, suggesting that Red Sox reliever Jovani Moran intentionally hit catcher Austin Wells with a pitch. He also asked Moran to start a fight with 2B Jazz Chisholm Jr. after repeatedly criticizing Chisholm as a bush-league player and alleging that he doesn't play the game the right way.

Judge addressed some media questions ahead of the series finale against the Angels in Anaheim on Monday, where he gave a blunt take on Flemming's comments toward Wells and Chisholm Jr.

"He needs to stay out of that and not be telling people to throw at players and injure players. That's not what this game's about. That game determines home field advantage in the playoffs. It's a six-run game. They get a couple guys on and hit a big homer, all of a sudden, we're getting our bullpen guys up and in a tight spot," Judge said.

"If you're not going to hold him on, what's going on here? Are you conceding, not conceding? What's going on? It's a six-run game. It's still a close ballgame. So yeah, not too happy hearing a broadcaster is talking about trying to injure and hurt a player. He needs to clean that up," he added.

Judge has yet to resume play in the field since being sidelined with a rib injury on May 31. While reports suggest his rehab process is progressing efficiently, the Bombers could get a boost with the addition of their club captain as the season enters its final stretch before October baseball comes calling.

Speaking to the media ahead of the series opener against the Halos on Monday, Yankees skipper Aaron Boone addressed multiple game-related questions, especially their resounding series win over Boston.

Furthermore, when asked about Judge's return timeline, Boone sounded optimistic, noting his star slugger's rehab progress and the possibility that he could return as early as the next homestand.

"He's doing well. He's here, you know. He's here to kind of continue to ramp up baseball activities. So, you know, we're getting closer, but feel good about where he's at. I think it's possible. I'm not going to put a date on it, but, you know, I think those things are in play now. It's, again, about getting the durability and the workload built up on him, which is the biggest thing now," Boone said.

The Yankees lost Monday's series opener to the Angels, 10-1, and will aim to bounce back in Game 2 on Tuesday night to avoid a series defeat.

After Los Angeles, the Bombers will travel to San Diego for a three-game series against the Padres, then head back to the Bronx to begin a six-game homestand against the Rockies and the Mets.

title: What kind of player is Balogun?
description: Everton have agreed a £40m deal to sign USA international Folarin Balogun from Monaco, with a medical set to take place on Tuesday.  A one-time Arsenal academy graduate, Balogun joined Monaco from the Gunners for £35m in 2023, going on to score 31 goals in 91 appearances for the Ligue 1 club. fullText:
Everton have agreed a £40m deal to sign USA international Folarin Balogun from Monaco, with a medical set to take place on Tuesday.

So what type of player will the Blues be signing and how does he compare with Thierno Barry, the Toffees' current first-choice striker?

A one-time Arsenal academy graduate, Balogun joined Monaco from the Gunners for £35m in 2023, going on to score 31 goals in 91 appearances for the Ligue 1 club.

He missed four months of the 2024-25 campaign due to injury but after returning to fitness in April he enjoyed the most prolific season of his career to date in 2025-26, scoring 19 goals in 43 games, including five in the Champions League.

Whereas Barry is more of a target man adept at winning balls in the air, Balogun boasts greater pace and a game built around making runs behind opposition defences.

At the World Cup earlier this summer, the 25-year-old averaged eight runs in behind per game, ranking him third of all strikers, and scored three goals.

His goals-per-minute ratio was almost identical to that of Beto, who is leaving Everton for Fiorentina in a £15m deal, in league football last season.

But Balogun's younger age and Champions League experience suggest his ceiling could be comparatively higher.

His tally of 19 goals last season is at least seven more than either Beto or Barry have managed in a campaign with a club in an elite European league.

title: Why Katie Taylor’s final fight at Croke Park is not about what happens in the ring
description: An Irish icon, Olympic gold medalist, and undisputed champion at two weights, Taylor finally realises her Croke Park dream this weekend – as she says farewell to boxing
fullText:
It took minutes to convince everybody that Katie Taylor truly did deserve a final fight in front of 80,000 people at Croke Park in Dublin on Saturday night.

The tickets went on sale and then the tickets for boxing's greatest final fight sold out; it was all over in 30 minutes of trading, and Taylor's position as one of the most popular fighters in history was secure.

The journey to the very end of the boxing line started so long ago when Taylor, with her hair in braids tucked inside a headguard, posed as a boy to have her first fight. A legend was born on a tiny amateur show, and the girl from Bray was on her way.

The battle for equality was on; Taylor moved through the ranks, became the star of the Irish boxing team, won medals in tournaments all over the world and then won the Olympic title in London in 2012.

At Dublin airport there are three giant pictures of iconic people arriving in the Irish capital; there is the pope, there is a smiling President John F Kennedy, and the final picture is a joyous shot of Taylor with her gold medal in her hand, smiling from the cockpit of a plane.

The hero was back from London that afternoon in the summer of 2012, and this Saturday that long road to glory will finish at the home of Irish sport. The sacred ground will belong to the small girl from Bray – it has been a dream all her boxing life.

Flora Pili, an unbeaten Frenchwoman, was picked for the final dance in the ring. The fight is for three versions of the super-lightweight title, but at this point in her remarkable career, all glittering baubles are an unnecessary distraction. Taylor has won so many and in so many fights; her ring genius is not measured by the amount of costume belts that can be strapped across her body.

Taylor is now 40 and this last fight will be her 21st consecutive world-title fight, a run that started in 2017; there was the one loss against Chantelle Cameron in Dublin 2023 and then the triumphant rematch victory a few months later.

She has dominated and led the revolution from the ground up; she was once the little girl pretending to be a boy to get a fight, and on Saturday she will be the multi-millionaire national hero walking to the ring on a bed of love and adoration to thank the faithful. It's a boxing fairytale, make no mistake.

For Saturday's fight, Taylor had the pick of any woman operating within a 10lb range of the 140lb limit, and there were dozens waiting for the call. In the end, it was Pili, fresh, unbeaten, and a safe choice for a fight and night when the opponent's credentials are irrelevant. Pili can make it difficult if Taylor is overwhelmed by emotion and the vastness of the event.

However, this is not about Taylor having one final test, one final great victory – it is all about the walk to the ring and saying goodbye, and 80,000 people howling and smiling and crying. There has never been a final fight in boxing history quite like this. A nation will stop for the tiny girl from Bray one last time.

title: ‘I’d Give Him a Quick Little $5,000’ — Hall of Famer Wants Quick Resolution on Odell Beckham Jr.’s Giants Roadblock
description: Wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. has officially returned to the New York Giants, in what is shaping up to be an exciting moment for fans who were reminiscing about his impact during his first stint with the franchise.
fullText:
Wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. has officially returned to the New York Giants, in what is shaping up to be an exciting moment for fans who were reminiscing about his impact during his first stint with the franchise. As he is now back on the Giants' 53-man roster, Beckham has another goal in mind: reclaiming his iconic No. 13 jersey.

That, however, may need some doing, considering Jalin Hyatt currently has his hands on the number. However, Hall of Famer Shannon Sharpe knows how Beckham can get his jersey number back.

Hyatt has worn No. 13 for the New York Giants over the past few seasons. However, he was recently waived by the team before being brought back to the practice squad.

That situation could make the jersey-number discussion much easier for Beckham. Since Hyatt is no longer part of the Giants' 53-man roster, the two could potentially settle the matter with a simple discussion.

Hyatt's production also doesn't quite match what Beckham accomplished while wearing No. 13 in New York. That could give Beckham another argument for reclaiming the jersey that became synonymous with him during his first stint with the Giants.

The topic came up during the latest episode of the"Nightcap" podcast. Co-host Chad Johnson suggested that practice-squad players should be willing to give up a jersey number when a former star associated with that number returns to the team.

Johnson explained that seeing #13 on a Giants uniform immediately reminds him of Beckham and everything the receiver accomplished during his first few seasons in the NFL.

Meanwhile, Sharpe offered a straightforward solution to OBJ's problem.

"I would give him (Hyatt) a quick little $5,000," Sharpe said.

When Johnson jokingly argued that Hyatt shouldn't be disrespected during the jersey-number debate, Sharpe fired back with an amusing response.

"He disrespected my jersey by getting it," Sharpe said. "You know you ain't supposed to get that jersey like that after what I did there the first 3-4 years of my career."

"I think we all know what that means to me," Beckham told reporters on Monday. "There definitely will be some conversations. I'll just say we'll see what happens. But, like I said, it would be an honor and a privilege to put that back on."

There is little doubt that No. 13 carries significant meaning for both Beckham and Giants fans. New York selected Beckham 12th overall in the 2014 NFL Draft, and he quickly established himself as one of the most electrifying wide receivers of his generation.

Beckham never won a Super Bowl with the Giants, but his first stint in New York was filled with individual accomplishments. He won Offensive Rookie of the Year and was named to three Pro Bowls.

title: Barcelona new signing compares La Liga with the Premier League – ‘Football here is different’
description: Anthony Gordon produced a stellar performance in the final third as Barcelona secured a comprehensive 5-2 win over Rayo Vallecano on Monday night.The summer signing from Newcastle United notably assis...
fullText:
Anthony Gordon produced a stellar performance in the final third as Barcelona secured a comprehensive 5-2 win over Rayo Vallecano on Monday night.

The summer signing from Newcastle United notably assisted one of the goals from Raphinha while also playing a crucial role in Florian Lejeune's own goal.

The Englishman demonstrated excellent chemistry with his teammates and appears to be settling in well in La Liga.

In the wake of his performance against Rayo, the forward tried to compare La Liga's brand of football with the Premier League.

Gordon acknowledged the intensity of English football but highlighted the different demands of Spanish football.

"I'm not going to deny that the Premier League is incredibly intense. The rhythm is relentless, there are physical battles everywhere, long band kicks, corner kicks and a lot of contact.

Gordon had an outstanding game vs Rayo. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

"That's why many English players believe it is the best league in the world. They're used to that kind of chaos," he said, as quoted by SPORT.

The Englishman then pointed out the nuances of Spanish football, especially in relation to the recent game against Rayo Vallecano.

"Football in Spain is different. Rayo retreated and tried to make the match difficult, something you also see in many mid-table Premier League teams. The difference is that we don't just resort to long balls or relying on ball-to-ball plays," he said.

Gordon praised Barcelona's style as the key differentiator, saying: "We moved the ball, Pedri found spaces between the lines, Lamine and the others created numerical superiority and patiently disarmed them with our football."

The forward also flagged the technical precision required in La Liga, as he said:

"In England, sometimes intensity can cover up mistakes. You can mis-control the ball and still recover by winning the next physical battle. Here, a bad first touch or a lack of concentration on your positioning can punish you immediately."

"The spaces are smaller, the decisions have to be faster and everything must be cleaner," he added.

Gordon's cross forced Lejeune's own goal. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Gordon believes the Spanish game actually enhances one of his biggest strengths.

"My speed becomes even more effective here because the movement around me creates opportunities and spaces, rather than everyone simply running forward in straight lines," he said.

At the same time, though, the Englishman was careful not to disrespect the league in which he grew up.

"I loved playing in the Premier League and it played a huge role in my development. But Spanish football demands a different level of tactical and technical intelligence," he said.

He did, however, offer an observation about how certain English sides would cope.

"Some Premier League teams would have a hard time playing this style consistently because they may not have the patience or quality in the midfield that is required."

"That's not disrespecting them, it's just what I've noticed in my first games. There's a different football intelligence here," Gordon concluded.

title: Serie A 2026/27: Inter Milan make a strong start to their title defence
description: The start of the 2026/27 Serie A season has generated plenty of talking points, particularly for the clubs with title aspirations.Six teams have an unblemished record after two games and four of them ...
fullText:
The start of the 2026/27 Serie A season has generated plenty of talking points, particularly for the clubs with title aspirations.

Six teams have an unblemished record after two games and four of them are teams who are expected to be battling to win the Scudetto this term.

Without further ado, read on as we look at how the Serie A title race is taking shape, starting with defending champions Inter Milan.

After recording an impressive 4-1 home victory over Monza in their opening game, Inter were made to work a little harder in their second outing at Cagliari.

Hakan Calhanoglu's long-range strike settled the game, but Cristian Chivu's side needed two decisive saves from Josep Martinez to seal the win.

Calhanoglu is now the only midfielder to have scored more than once in each of the last 14 seasons across Europe's top five leagues, highlighting his importance to the team.

However, Martinez arguably stole the show, making a pair of excellent stops in the second half to keep the home side at bay.

Yann Bisseck also stepped up when it mattered, heading a goal-bound effort over the bar as Cagliari desperately fought to equalise.

Inter's ability to sig deep when they are under pressure is an attribute which should serve them extremely well as the season progresses.

A pair of hugely impressive 4-0 victories over Fiorentina and Lecce in their first two fixtures have fired Roma to the top of the Serie A standings.

Donyell Malen has been a standout performer, scoring five goals in two games. He has now bagged 19 goals in 20 league appearances since joining the club from Aston Villa.

Having guided Roma to third place in Serie A last season, manager Gian Piero Gasperini is eager to knock Inter off their perch this time around.

Gasperini's team are entertaining to watch when they are in full flow, but it is too early to determine whether they are genuine title contenders.

The upcoming home game against Atalanta will provide a useful indicator of their title hopes. They are also scheduled to host Inter Milan this month.

If Roma can reach the international break with their unbeaten record intact, it would be impossible to dismiss their chances of winning the Scudetto.

Former Manchester United Ruben Amorim has made a solid start to life in Serie A by guiding AC Milan to victories over Torino and Venezia.

However, it would be fair to categorise Milan as 'a work in progress' and it will be intriguing to see how they fare when they face one of the top teams.

Striker Goncalo Ramos got off the mark for the season against Venezia, but he will need to be more clinical if Milan are to mount a sustained title challenge.

His wastefulness in front of goal kept Venezia in the game, and Amorim will be concerned by how often they breached Milan's defence.

Visits to Juventus and Lazio in their next two games will demonstrate whether Milan have what it takes to stay in the title race this season.

Intriguingly, Christian Pulisic and Diego Moreira have yet to feature this term, so the level of performances could increase when they are integrated into the team.

Juventus have been steady rather than spectacular in their first two games, defeating Frosinone and Parma without conceding a goal.

Luciano ​Spalletti's side wasted plenty of decent opportunities against Parma, but eventually got the job done courtesy of Teun Koopmeiners late effort.

After buying extremely well during the summer transfer window, Juventus look well-placed to mount a sustained title challenge this season.

Atalanta and Lazio are the only other Serie A teams with a 100 percent record after two games, but neither appeal as potential Scudetto winners.

La Dea were extremely fortunate to beat Bologna in their second outing, while Lazio's lack of firepower is still a major issue.

Napoli suffered a defeat in their second outing against Como, but should be capable of forcing their way into contention over the coming weeks.

Inter were worthy champions last season and they will be a tough nut to crack this time around.

Roma could keep themselves in contention under Gasperini, but Milan may be the biggest threat to the defending champions this term.

title: Lyon winger Fofana set for £30m Sunderland move
description: Sunderland agree a deal worth just under £30m for Lyon winger Malick Fofana, who is set to sign a five-year contract.
fullText:
Sunderland have agreed a deal worth just under £30m for Lyon winger Malick Fofana.

The 21-year-old is travelling to England for a medical and is expected to sign a five-year contract.

The deal for the Belgium forward will cost an initial £25.6m, with a potential £4.3m in add-ons.

Fofana is understood to be excited by the prospect of joining Sunderland before their first European campaign in 51 years, having qualified for the Europa League.

The move follows attempts by Arsenal to sign Fofana, but the Premier League champions were unable to agree a fee with Lyon.

Fofana began his career at KAA Gent before joining the Ligue 1 side in 2024.

He is set to join Kevin Danso at Sunderland, with the Austria defender due to arrive from Tottenham on an initial loan with an option to buy.

Sunderland have also signed defenders Thomas Meunier and Dayann Methalie, and midfielder Jules Ahoka, this summer after finishing seventh in their first season back in the top flight.

title: Drama continues in Pakistan cricket: Misbah-ul-Haq resigns from PCB selection committee after 7 players were sent home from England tour
description: Misbah-ul-Haq has resigned from the PCB selection committee after reportedly being bypassed over the decision to send 7 players home from the England Test tour.
fullText:

Misbah-ul-Haq has reportedly stepped down from the PCB's selection committee.

Misbah's decision comes a day after Pakistan sent back seven players from their Test squad in the middle of the England series.

Misbah was reportedly unhappy with the decision to make changes in the squad in the middle of a series.

Misbah-ul-Haq has walked away from his role on the PCB selection committee after seven Test players were abruptly pulled out of the England tour following the 194-run defeat at Lord's.

According to The Express Tribune, Misbah has already submitted his resignation letter to the board. He's expected to work through a notice period before officially stepping away from the role.

What seems to have triggered this was the PCB's decision to release seven players from the squad following the crushing loss at Lord's, bringing in fresh faces for the series finale at Edgbaston instead.

MORE: Has any team made drastic changes to their squad in the middle of a series before?

Misbah, despite sitting on the selection committee, was reportedly left completely out of the loop on how and why those calls were made, and that exclusion clearly didn't sit well with him.

Moreover, Sarfaraz Ahmed lost his job as red-ball head coach, and Umar Gul was also relieved of his fast-bowling coach duties. White-ball head coach Mike Hesson, alongside bowling coach Ashley Noffke, have been asked to step in to steady things for the Edgbaston Test as the board didn't have many options left with the series on the line.

MORE: Five times Pakistan shocked the cricket world: Instances when PCB took weird calls

Misbah's association with the panel only goes back to March 2026, when the PCB revamped the committee after Aleem Dar stepped down following a rough T20 World Cup campaign. Sarfaraz had joined the selection setup around the same time, before later taking the red-ball coaching job on April 18.

It was just ahead of a two-Test tour of Bangladesh that Pakistan lost 2-0. A subsequent series against West Indies ended in a 1-1 draw, hardly the platform of stability the team needed heading into England.

Now, with Pakistan 2-0 down and facing a series whitewash at Edgbaston, the mounting results pressure appears to have finally cracked the working relationships behind the scenes.

MORE: Pakistan's head coach and captain merry-go-round: Are the players scapegoats?

Misbah's resignation isn't really surprising once you look at the pattern here. Pakistan cricket has a long, tiring habit of making major calls without proper consultation, then acting shocked when senior figures walk out the door.

When you sideline a sitting selector from such an important decision as sending seven players home mid-series isn't just poor etiquette; it's a structural failure. You can't build a functioning selection process if half the committee finds out about major moves after they've already happened.

MORE: 'T20 players included for Tests': Afridi, Malik blasts PAK selectors over squad selection

This kind of chaos doesn't just cost Pakistan on the field, though that's bad enough with a whitewash now looming. It corrodes trust among the very people meant to steer the team through rough patches. Until PCB fixes how decisions actually get made, rather than just reshuffling names in and out of jobs, these resignations and walkouts are only going to keep piling up.

title: Giants' Malik Nabers 'feels good,' but won't commit to Week 1 return
description: New York Giants WR Malik Nabers says he feels good, even "real good," but won't commit to playing in Week 1.
fullText:
One of the big questions surrounding the New York Giants this summer is whether their No. 1 wide receiver, Malik Nabers, will be ready for the regular season.

With 12 days until the Giants' opener against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football at MetLife Stadium, the question remains unanswered.

Nabers tore his ACL and meniscus last October and had a complicated rehab after surgery. He then needed a second surgery this spring to "clean up" scar tissue.

Nabers told reporters on Monday that he's not sure if he'll play in the opener, but he's doing everything he can to get ready.

"My mind is focused on playing the regular season, playing whenever that is and playing what team it is," he said. "I'm going to be making sure that I'm ready to go out there and I'm healthy enough to play all four quarters. That nobody got to make sure I'm not in on every play, or they have to make sure I got enough snaps or my snaps are limited. So, that's the main focus is just trying to be out there as much as I can."

The decision is not all Nabers' to make. The Giants' medical and training staff have to sign off on his return to 100 percent participation.

"I feel pretty good. Well, I feel real good, to be honest. But like I said, you're going to feel good, but there's still some things that you still have to check off the box for you to participate," said Nabers. "So, I'm still going through that, still listening to the trainers, still listening to doctors and sharing everything with them."

What checkpoints was he speaking of?

"I'm going to keep the checkpoints in-house. It's not really anything too big, but as I said, I'm going to keep it more in-house and just to myself."

title: Where is the Detroit Lions’ 53-man roster’s biggest weakness?
description: Scanning the Detroit Lions’ 53-man roster for their biggest needs and weaknesses.
fullText:
Forming a 53-man roster is a never-ending business in the NFL. The Detroit Lions may have settled on an initial 53-man roster and 15 of their 16 practice squad players, but general manager Brad Holmes and the rest of the Lions' personnel department are not "finished."

The job of an NFL personnel employee is never done. The search for upgrades at every position continues throughout the entire season. Whether it's free agency, the waiver wire, the NFL Draft, the trade deadline, or any other time of year, there is a humongous pool of football talent available, and opportunities abound.

That job never ends, because no NFL roster is perfect. There are holes, depth issues, injury insurance needed, and new players who just don't end up working out. The Detroit Lions are no exception to this.

You better believe that this week the Lions will continue to look across the NFL landscape and hundreds of newly available players and see if they can upgrade their team. But before they do that, they need to evaluate the status of their own roster. So today's Question of the Day is:

My answer: I think my answer is the same it was when the Lions entered training camp: cornerback.

While I've certainly been encouraged by the play of starters D.J. Reed and Rock Ya-Sin thus far, I haven't had that same level of optimism with the depth. Ennis Rakestraw had a very up-and-down camp with more downs than ups. Roger McCreary, who I believed to be a savvy pickup, has had flashes (particularly in the first two preseason games), but has underwhelmed from my previous expectations. The most promising player amongst the depth is Nick Whiteside, and Detroit didn't even believe he played well enough to warrant a spot on the 53-man roster, risking losing him by putting him on waivers before bringing him back to the practice squad.

The situation at nickel may be even more dire. While things were trending toward Christian Izien winning the starting job before his injury, that felt more like no one winning the job than anything. McCreary didn't stand out. Rakestraw was kept on the outside. And rookie Keith Abney is clearly still adjusting to being a full-time nickel after having more success on the outside in college. Not only do I not know who the starter at nickel will be in Week 1, I'm not sure who the best possible reserve is, either.

I say all of this not to induce panic. I'm actually a pretty big fan of the rest of this roster, and if the Lions can get plenty of healthy playing time out of Reed and Ya-Sin, maybe they'll hold up at cornerback, too.

But if I were Holmes and company, I'd certainly keep my ears and eyes open to upgrading the cornerback room.

title: Phillies Offer Frustrating 3-Word Update On Stymied Shortstop Aidan Miller
description: Philadelphia Phillies’ executive Dave Dombrowski sent a brief message about the top prospect following an unfortunate injury setback.
fullText:
The Philadelphia Phillies have already received meaningful contributions from some of their top prospects this season, with Justin Crawford and Andrew Painter making the jump to the major leagues and earning lasting roles as the team tries to earn another National League East title this season.

With a top-heavy farm system, the Phillies don't have much exciting prospect depth, but both players were seen as very likely to make their debuts this year after strong minor league campaigns in 2025.

"Painter was a lock to make the team with Zack Wheeler recovering from thoracic outlet decompression surgery," Todd Zolecki wrote for MLB.com. "Crawford was a lock with the organization parting ways with center fielder Harrison Bader."

Another highly regarded prospect who once seemed to be a lock for promotion this year has instead watched his season disappear before it ever really began.

Red Sox Owner Makes Conspicuous Change In Tumultuous Season

Phillies top prospect Aidan Miller has been sidelined by a persistent back problem, leaving fans frustrated as they wait to see what the prized infielder can do at the upper levels of the organization.

In early June, the team announced a concerning setback for the young shortstop which further delayed his ability to make any progress toward a debut. He was diagnosed with discogenic pain and facet inflammation in his lumbar spine, requiring a procedure and significant recovery. At the time, the team indicated he would be able to return to game activity in six to eight weeks.

"The infielder has not played in a game this year," NBC Sports Philadelphia's Cole Weintraub noted at the time of that announcement. "The back issue kept him out of Grapefruit League action and delayed what was expected to be his first full season at Triple-A."

With that procedure scheduled to take place more than two months ago, it would seem that the team might have a more promising update to share with fans on Miller's progress. But that doesn't seem to be the case.

Yankees World Series Infielder Sends Retirement Message, 'Coolest Memory'

The latest update from Phillies president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski offered little clarity on when Miller might get back onto a diamond.

"Continuing to progress," Dombrowski said late last week Friday when asked about the top ranked prospect, according to The Athletic's Matt Gelb and Charlotte Varnes.

That three-word response might be encouraging on the surface, as progress is important, but it also suggests Miller is not all that close to playing in meaningful games.

While Crawford has provided the Phillies with another athletic option in the outfield and Painter has managed to recover from a slow start to eat some significant innings, Miller was supposed to be part of that next wave, too.

Instead, his development still appears to be stuck in a holding pattern according to the latest update likely to frustrate fans.

title: Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo’s World Cup records compared as international rivalry ends

title: ‘The league’s a disaster right now’: Mike Francesa calls out WNBA
description: It’s been a wild summer for the WNBA, between the seemingly endless controversies involving Caitlin Clark and all of the political firestorm that ensued after Sophie Cunningham spoke out against transgender women in women’s sports. fullText:
It's been a wild summer for the WNBA, between the seemingly endless controversies involving Caitlin Clark and all of the political firestorm that ensued after Sophie Cunningham spoke out against transgender women in women's sports. While it's certainly led to a lot of media attention, it isn't exactly good attention.

Over the past few months, the WNBA has become the most toxic space in all sports as players and the league itself have become political pawns. Now, longtime radio host Mike Francesa is calling out the league's leadership.

During his podcast this week, Mike Francesa was asked his take on the current state of the WNBA, and he was certainly not shy about blaming the WNBA's leadership for not having the foresight to see how things would change once Clark entered the league and the players for not welcoming her.

"They have turned their league into a bubbling, volcanic, political, chaotic situation where every nut is now getting involved politically in the WNBA on all different levels," Francesa ranted on his podcast. "It's the worst thing that could have ever happened. I blame the people who run the league, I blame the players who didn't have the long-range vision and didn't have the smarts to realize what Caitlin Clark was going to do for their league, and instead, tried to hurt her and run her out of the league at every point."

Francesa went on to compare Clark to when Pete Maravich joined the Atlanta Hawks.

"There were revolts against Pete Maravich when he came to the NBA," Francesa recalled. "He broke up a very good Atlanta Hawks team because there was insane jealousy and people felt he hadn't earned anything and they felt he was just a self-promoting showboat."

While the issues might have started with Clark, Francesa acknowledges that the issues are far beyond her at this point.

"Caitlin Clark came to that league and energized it in a way that they had never seen possible," Francesa added.  "They had never been able to sell that league to anybody, and she sold it to everybody. And they're all trying to ruin it. And now it's become a political mess way past just the issues with Caitlin Clark. The league's a disaster right now."

title: Scottie Scheffler sets new PGA Tour record by achieving feat no other player in history has managed
description: Scottie Scheffler finished his 2026 PGA Tour season in style on Sunday at East Lake. Scheffler won the Tour Championship by three strokes after shooting a final-round 66, and he secured his second FedEx Cup trophy in the process.
fullText:
Scottie Scheffler finished his 2026 PGA Tour season in style on Sunday at East Lake.

Scheffler won the Tour Championship by three strokes after shooting a final-round 66, and he secured his second FedEx Cup trophy in the process.

The 30-year-old world number one ended the PGA Tour season with three wins.

While that represents somewhat of a drop-off for Scottie Scheffler, his numbers are actually even better than last season.

He recorded the lowest ever scoring average in PGA Tour history this season.

Meanwhile, Scheffler is now fifth on the all-time PGA Tour win percentage list, behind only Tiger Woods, Ben Hogan, Byron Nelson and Sam Snead.

At the Tour Championship on Sunday, though, Scheffler achieved a feat that no other player in history has managed.

It's fair to argue that Scheffler is already one of the greatest golfers in the history of the sport.

In order to become one of the best four or five golfers of all-time, though, he will need to continue doing what he's doing for the next 5-10 years.

That said, he has already broken two PGA Tour records.

However, one of them is far more meaningful than the other.

Scheffler became the career money leader on the PGA Tour on Sunday, but that one doesn't hold that much weight, considering the recent purse increases.

However, another record that he has now broken does have genuine meaning.

Scheffler's win at the Tour Championship on Sunday saw him top the money list for the fifth consecutive season.

Even Tiger Woods or Jack Nicklaus were unable to manage that.

Topping the PGA Tour money list for five consecutive seasons is a record that Scottie Scheffler can be truly proud of.

It is evidence of his remarkably consistent brilliance.

The worrying thing for his rivals is that he doesn't seem to be slowing down either.

There's a good chance that in 10 years' time, we will be talking about Scottie Scheffler as one of the genuine greats of the game.

The world number one just needs to remain hungry to keep getting better and there is no doubt that he will end up compiling one of the most successful PGA Tour careers of all time.

title: Musiala close to Bayern comeback, possibly already in Cup game
description: German international Jamal Musiala is close to his comeback at Bayern Munich and may even feature in Wednesday's German Cup match at third division Osnabrück, coach Vincent Kompany has said. fullText:
German international Jamal Musiala is close to his comeback at Bayern Munich and may even feature in Wednesday's German Cup match at third division Osnabrück, coach Vincent Kompany has said.

Musiala collapsed due to absence seizures in two pre-season friendlies and had to sit out the start to the season while his medication was adjusted.

Kompany said on Tuesday that there will be talks with Musiala and doctors before a decision whether Musiala can return on Wednesday, in Saturday's Bundesliga match at Schalke or next week in the Champions League against Bodø/Glimt.

"He's trained very well. It's a question of choosing the right moment; whether that's tomorrow, at the weekend or next week, I can't yet say," Kompany.

Kompany added that forward Serge Gnabry is also about to return from a thigh muscle injury he sustained in spring and made him miss the World Cup, but not yet for the Cup game.

Jonas Urbig will meanwhile be in goal for the title holders on Wednesday instead of Manuel Neuer as the youngster continues to get playing time as Neuer's career winds down.

"We've already put an incredible amount of trust in Jonas. He's played in many important matches, such as the cup final. These are milestones that show he can perform in big games," Kompany said.

Bayern are big favourites against Osnabrück but Kompany said they won't underestimate them.

"These matches are usually tough. That's part and parcel of the cup competition. You have to be mentally prepared for a real battle," he said.

"When we're on form, things often click. But it always depends on how quickly you can find the spaces and how dangerous they can become," he said.

The overall goal is however clear for the domestic double winners.

"Once you've been in the final, you always want to get there again. Our opponents were Stuttgart; they'd reached the final twice in a row. We want to achieve that now too," Kompany said.

title: Wrexham close in on Sheffield Utd's O'Hare

fullText:

O'Hare is set to undergo a medical at the north Wales club with a view to completing a permanent move worth around £6.5m.

fullText:
The transfer deadline day is finally here, but for Real Madrid, who have been quite active all throughout summer, are largely expected to remain unbothered.

The club are handling only one or two deals on the departures' side, with Manuel Angel soon expected to close his move to Fulham.

That said, Real Madrid would be keeping an eye on one deal that might lead to a slight economic boost on the deadline day.

As reported by Mundo Deportivo, Real Madrid will be keeping a close eye on Sergio Arribas today.

Sergio Arribas has been in top form since joining Almeria. (Photo by Rafa Babot/Getty Images)

The former Real Madrid youth player, who currently plays for Almeria, is reportedly closing in on a move to SL Benfica.

With 25 goals and seven assists in La Liga 2 last season, Arribas has impressed greatly at Almeria and Benfica are keen on acquiring his services.

The player hasn't trained with the team, sparking rumours of a late departure. He does have a release clause worth €40 million, which makes the saga even more interesting.

Real Madrid will be watching the saga closely as the club currently hold 50% of the player's transfer rights.

Can Benfica manage a late swoop for Arribas? (Photo by Rafa Babot/Getty Images)

That means the club are entitled to half the proceeds of Arribas' potential transfer value.

With Arribas having a €40 million release clause, Real Madrid would ideally be hoping for a €20 million windfall. However, Benfica have no desire to match his release clause.

The Portuguese giants are expected to negotiate and try lowering the overall deal value, which does also translate to a lower fee for Real Madrid.

Almeria are expected to contest it and negotiate hard, knowing the club can only obtain half of the agreed deal value.

So it will be interesting to see how things unfold as Benfica make a late attempt to sign one of La Liga 2's most exciting players.

title: ‘I didn’t want to play very long’ – Joe Burrow addresses potential retirement timeline before season
description: Cincinnati Bengals QB Joe Burrow revealed his potential timeline for retirement from the NFL after admitting he never wanted to have a long career. Burrow has been a star in the NFL since entering the league as the No.
fullText:
Cincinnati Bengals QB Joe Burrow revealed his potential timeline for retirement from the NFL after admitting he never wanted to have a long career.

Burrow has been a star in the NFL since entering the league as the No. 1 pick in the 2020 NFL Draft. Heading into Year 6, Burrow is regarded as one of the best in his position.

While retirement is definitely not something anyone expects the 29-year-old to do anytime soon, he did speak candidly about what his initial plans were and how he views his career now.

In an interview with Albert Breer, Burrow admitted he wanted to retire early but now feels like he will play until his body does not allow him to do it anymore.

"I used to think I didn't want to play very long, and now I'm like, I'm just going to go until I can't do it anymore. This is fun to do. What the hell else would I do?"

While Tom Brady is an unfair comparison, we did see him play until he was 45 years old. LeBron James is playing a different sport in the NBA, but even he is gearing up to play a 24th season at 42 years old.

Aaron Rodgers is suiting up for his 22nd and final NFL season this year; Aaron Donald just returned from retirement, and even Phillip Rivers returned to the field at 45 years old last season to play for the Colts.

If it's about playing until he physically cannot, Burrow could have well over a decade more to offer fans, barring any catastrophic injury.

It's just a question of how Burrow deals with the inevitable decline in athleticism QBs face in their 30s, and at what level of production he wants to step away from the field.

His decision will also be informed by how, when, or if he wins a Super Bowl in his career. At least Bengals fans can rest assured that their star QB intends to spend more time playing than he initially did.

title: Falkirk must 'dig heels in' to keep Spencer

fullText:
Following our exploits over the past three years, particularly last season, it was always going to be difficult to retain all of our best players this summer.

That's the reality for clubs like Falkirk. When you have got good players, you have to enjoy them while they are here and accept that other clubs will eventually come calling.

Barney Stewart and Calvin Miller certainly fell into that category and both departed this summer with everyone's best wishes.

Brad Spencer is another who continues to be linked with a move away, but losing him at this stage of the transfer window would be a real hammer blow.

He might not have grabbed the headlines like Stewart or Miller, but you could argue he's been even more important to us. For three years, he has anchored our midfield and been at the heart of a side that's taken us from League 1 to the Premiership.

That's why selling him now would send out completely the wrong message.

Losing Spencer would be a major blow at any stage, but doing so this late in the window would leave us precious little time to replace him.

He still has a couple of years remaining on his contract and, unless an offer arrives that's simply impossible to refuse, I would want us to dig our heels in.

John McGlynn has hinted one more player could arrive before the window closes, but I'd rather we used whatever is left in the budget to top up Spencer's wages than bring in someone to replace him. That's how important he is to us.

It's going to be a nervous few days for us Bairns.

And with Falkirk heading to Tannadice on Saturday, you can't help wondering which team Spencer will be playing for.

title: Mikel Arteta gives injury update after Arsenal star forced off in win over Aston Villa
description: Cristhian Mosquera was taken off in the second half on Monday as Ezri Konsa made his Arsenal debut against his former club
fullText:
Mikel Arteta has confirmed that Cristhian Mosquera is "fine" after the Spanish defender was substituted during Arsenal's 1-0 victory at Aston Villa on Monday night.

The Arsenal manager chose not to risk the 22-year-old, introducing new signing Ezri Konsa late on, who faced jeers on his return to Villa Park.

"We knew that if we had an injury on the back line with Jurrien (Timber) out, we'd be in big trouble – so we had to do Ezri," Arteta explained post-match, after Bukayo Saka's second-half goal secured two Premier League wins from two for the champions.

"Mosquera could not continue, so we know the depth has to be really big when we're fighting for four competitions in the manner that we play as well.

"He's fine, but he was feeling like he was about to have something, and that's why we have the bench that we have, and that's why we had to bring Ezri in.

"Ezri makes a debut in really difficult circumstances; it's not easy emotionally to come here and play. But he looks so composed, so calm, so in control."

Riccardo Calafiori noted that securing the outcome mattered more than the overall performance as the Gunners completed the job.

It proved far from a classic performance, with Arsenal scoring from their first effort on target shortly before the hour, yet they ground out a hard-fought victory.

"I'm so happy with the clean sheet, especially when I talk with the guys – the defenders – I always say that if we don't concede, we obviously have much more chance to win the game, and I think we always do so well," the full-back said.

"At the end of the game, it's so important for us, especially at a tough place like this one, we just want to win when we come here and we did it.

"In pre-season we were upset, I think we conceded too much, but then as the season started, we have all the players back.

"We fight, and you see how we do mistakes sometimes, but how we track back with the runs, it's unbelievable, and each player, even the attackers, so I'm so happy."

Calafiori set up Saka's deciding goal to record his second assist of the campaign.

"I'm just so happy to pass the ball to B [Saka]," the 24-year-old Italy international added.

"As I say, it was a tough, tough game, we need these kind of moments, you know, to change the game – and we did it."

fullText:
Last month, Microsoft’s gaming division told its workforce it was cutting 3,200 jobs, which some say will have big ramifications for game development – as well as taking a huge personal toll

On the morning of 6 July, an email went out from Asha Sharma, the chief executive of Xbox, to all of the division’s employees around the world. Under the headline “Resetting Xbox”, it announced the most significant restructuring in the history of Microsoft’s console business: 3,200 staff would be laid off throughout the financial year to 2027, and 1,600 of those roles would be eliminated immediately.

An hour later, at studios throughout company, the Teams meeting invites started arriving. “It was a virtual call with our studio manager,” says Anne Barrett, who was laid off from Bethesda Game Studios Austin. “All of our cameras and microphones were turned off so we weren’t able to say anything or react to anything. We were just brought in, told the news and it was like: ‘You guys are going to lose access to your Slack channel.’ So you saw a flurry of goodbye messages before everything was just shut off.”

This, it seems, was the routine, at least at studios in North America: a Teams call with a studio head, a prepared statement read, then a warning about Slack (the group messaging app widely used at game development studios). Emails, the staff were told, would be turned off a few days later. “We’re primarily a remote studio, so Slack is the main mode of conversation with our teammates,” says Morgan Goin, who worked at ZeniMax Online Studios. “All through the morning, everyone was sending their goodbyes … ‘Hey, it’s been great working with you. Here’s my contact information. I’ve loved working here. I will miss all of you.’” Then silence.

Bethesda Games Studios and Zenimax Online Studios were unionised in 2024 and both Goin and Barrett are on the bargaining committees for their respective studios, currently in talks with Microsoft. In the US, the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) act is a federal law that requires companies with 100 or more employees to give its workers 60 days’ notice before major closures or mass staff layoffs. Consequently, affected staff at US studios will be paid until 4 September. Union reps at Bethesda are undertaking a bargaining process with Microsoft to negotiate severance packages and any benefits owed, and is attempting to get at least some affected members re-employed. Rallies are taking place outside studio buildings across North America, with the Bethesda union seeking support from gamers via social media.

Staff say rumours had been circulating about a new wave of lay-offs for several weeks, and that they saw the Bloomberg article on 10 June warning of coming job cuts. “There was an impending sense of doom, and it was like, man, is it going to be us?” says Barrett. “We thought we were safe. I mean, Bethesda Games Studios is Skyrim, it’s Fallout. We have really highly anticipated stuff coming out. We thought that the work we were doing was going to keep us safe. And instead, we got brought into a meeting that was two minutes long, to end, in some cases, decades of career at the company. It was just devastating.”

“I remember, I laughed the whole day because I was in complete disbelief,” Barrett adds. “I was like, there’s no way they’re doing this. That’s how I processed it. Some of my co-workers were just devastated. I mean, breaking down. They did not understand what was going on. We had people who were just in really dark places. I think it hit me probably the next day. I felt like, wow – I just spent seven years doing all this. In college, people called me Bethesda because it was my dream to work here. And that was just … gone.”

This is what doesn’t get reported with the statistics of mass redundancies: the sheer human cost of it. “I’m very tired, my sleep schedule is all kinds of messed up, my eating has not been great,” says Goin. “I have to ask myself daily: have you had enough food and water? Have you had enough sunlight? When was the last time you took a shower? We’re doing the depression symptoms, that’s what’s happening. I feel like I’m grieving.”

Simon Préfontaine has a similar story. Previously a designer at Bethesda Game Studios Montreal, he is a single father concerned about the future without work, and without the health insurance his job came with. “It’s very stressful,” he says. “I’ve heard of other people who have been laid off for over a year and haven’t been able to find work. I know I’m not the only single parent in the Montreal studio, I know there are people that have health issues.” But as with Goin, it is about more than financial stability. “It might seem like an overstatement or a dramatisation, but I do feel like I went through the stages of grief. You work with these people for years and years and years, and then suddenly you don’t get to see them any more.”

What has been most bewildering to staff is that there seemed to be no structure to the layoffs, no clear reasoning behind who was affected. “I’m on the character art team, and we lost two people who had been there for decades,” says Alex Nguyen, a union bargainer still employed at Bethesda Games Studios Dallas. “They did everything that was asked, they were very passionate, they were great at their jobs. They worked on all this stuff that made our creatures, characters and armour feel real. Outstanding employees. It never made any sense.”

It is likely, after all that, there will be ramifications for games being produced at these studios – including content delays and project cancellations. Id Software, creator of Doom and Quake, lost 136 staff in the cuts – a majority of its workforce. One staff member affected, VFX artist Derek Best, claimed in a LinkedIn post that the developer had been relegated to “support studio size”.

Barrett makes a similar assertion about Bethesda, where the redundancies have been less severe but where key staff have been affected. “I don’t know how you create games at the quality level we were without the institutional knowledge that’s been lost. We have proprietary tech. Our titles have a very well-known visual identity. And when you lose the people who built the tech, when you lose the people who were improving it, you can’t just throw new people at that problem, right? You can’t replace an artist with someone brand new and say: ‘Now replicate what they were doing 15, 20 years ago.’ The company has said that they can do it. I disagree.”

Nobody knows what happens next. Barrett could only provide a brief statement on how the union’s talks with Microsoft are faring: “Effects bargaining continues with each side exchanging counterproposals. In their counter, the employer has not made enough substantial movement to care for the very real consequences impacted members are facing (loss of employment; loss of income; and disruption of benefits for their families). We (the union) have indicated that we are prepared to work toward an agreement but we cannot accept a proposal where the burden of compromise falls almost entirely on the employees.”

A Microsoft spokesperson provided the following statement on the bargaining process: “Effects bargaining for our union-represented ZeniMax colleagues is under way and on track, and we have offered severance terms comparable to the generous package provided to our non-union represented colleagues, including up to 39 weeks of severance, six months of company-paid Cobra [Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act], and 16 weeks of outplacement support. We are committed to reaching an agreement that supports impacted colleagues as they move forward.”

At least 1,600 more redundancies are coming at Xbox studios as the “reset” of the division continues. During that time, there will likely be mass lay-off events at other large companies in the industry. All of the staff I spoke to echoed a familiar feeling about mainstream games development – that something has gone drastically wrong and that mass redundancies point to a wider malaise. “Publishers have to be prepared for multi-year development cycles,” says Nguyen. “If that cost is too high, or those timelines are too long, then the game needs to scale back in some way. That might mean more indie and AA games and fewer blockbuster titles. What doesn’t work is investing in a long-term game product, and expecting profits on a yearly basis.”

Barrett concurs. “My view of the industry has definitely been damaged,” she says. “There’s been a loss of sight over why AAA games were so valuable to players. It wasn’t just that they were big and shiny. It was that [the studios] had the resources to invest in creativity. What I see now is the same formula over and over and over again. In any entertainment industry, if you do that enough times, people get tired of it. I would love for us as an industry to get back to actually being creative and investing in that creativity.”

title: FIRST ON FOX: Texas becomes testing ground for new defense against attacks on America’s water systems
description: Project Watershed 250 pairs AI security tools with Texas water systems to find cyber vulnerabilities before adversaries can exploit them first.
fullText:
FIRST ON FOX: The Trump administration is launching "Project Watershed 250" Monday, Fox News Digital exclusively learned, deploying American artificial intelligence and cybersecurity tools to protect Texas water systems from cyberattacks in a pilot the administration plans to scale nationwide.

"Project Watershed 250 is another example of President Trump putting American families and communities first. President Trump is relentless in his work to secure our critical infrastructure against our most determined adversaries," National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross told Fox News Digital. "President Trump has cemented America's leadership in AI security and innovation and is now bringing those exquisite tools to local communities and utilities in Texas and ultimately, across the nation through the launch of Project Watershed 250 – a scalable cyber water pilot program."

The Trump administration is bringing federal, state and private-sector cyber defenses together in a six-month Texas pilot aimed at finding vulnerabilities in water systems before adversaries can exploit them — while testing whether the model can be expanded across the country.

Investigators Believe Iranian Hackers Are Likely Behind Cyberattack On Minnesota Water Systems: Report

The program will connect Texas water utilities with U.S. cybersecurity companies to test their existing defenses and strengthen vulnerable systems using private-sector cyber and artificial intelligence tools, a White House official told Fox News Digital.

The program will use "red-teaming" to stress-test water utilities' networks, identify weaknesses hackers could exploit and then strengthen those systems with cybersecurity tools, according to a White House official.

Trump Launches Gold Eagle To Hunt Cyber Flaws With Ai

Dragos CEO Robert Lee said that U.S. water infrastructure faces active, documented threats, particularly at small utilities that often lack strong cybersecurity defenses. Lee said Watershed 250 will help get technology, training and support to those vulnerable systems before an attack occurs.

"There is nothing more important to Texans than clean, reliable drinking water. Project Watershed 250 puts federal, state, and private-sector cyber defenses behind our utilities at no cost. The White House, the Texas Cyber Command, and industry now work from the same playbook," said Texas Gov. Greg Abbott.

A White House official, however, said the program is not in response to recent cyberattacks that targeted more than 30 Minnesota water systems, though the incidents underscored vulnerabilities in local infrastructure.

"However, these recent attacks have reiterated the need for this modernization and focus on water systems," said the White House official. "Critical Infrastructure protection has long been a priority for ONCD and President Trump and this effort has been in the works since last year."

Iranian Hackers Attacked Our Water Systems. Here Are 5 Things Our Leaders Need To Do Now

The Environmental Protection Agency and Department of Homeland Security's Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency will serve as federal partners in the effort, while Texas Cyber Command will work alongside the White House with local governments and tech companies such as Microsoft, Reflection AI, Palo Alto Networks and Dragos Inc.

"Few things matter more than the safety of the water Americans drink, and this is a powerful example of how open-weight AI models, built in the U.S. and running on a utility's own systems, can help keep communities safe," said Becky Sosnov, Reflection AI head of corporate affairs.

Anthropic's Mythos Ai Found Over 2,000 Unknown Software Vulnerabilities In Just Seven Weeks Of Testing

China-linked Hackers Infiltrated Us Government Networks Before Fbi Takedown

"Microsoft applauds the administration's leadership in strengthening the cybersecurity of America's water infrastructure and is proud to support the Project Watershed 250 effort in partnership with the Office of the National Cyber Director, the State of Texas, and Texas Cyber Command," said Microsoft US Public Sector president Chris Barry. "By bringing together Microsoft's cybersecurity expertise, threat intelligence, and AI-powered security capabilities, we aim to help water utilities strengthen their resilience against evolving cyber threats and develop scalable approaches that can enhance the security of water systems nationwide."

The push comes as the Trump administration races to build out U.S. data centers to fuel the AI boom, putting more attention on the water and power needed to keep them running.

The pilot program builds on Trump's June executive order on Promoting Advanced Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Security and his Cyber Strategy for America released in March.

title: 'I've never been to Afghanistan': Six million deportees forced to start over under the Taliban
description: As of August, the number forced to return this year from Pakistan and Iran had reached another million.
fullText:
The elderly grimace, hobbling on crutches, and wide-eyed children stare, cradling chickens carried from homes they were forced to leave behind.

"It feels good to be in my own country," 35-year-old Nazia says, just minutes after she crosses from Pakistan, where she was born, into Afghanistan.

The Torkham crossing, known as "Zero Point", is where one hard life ends and another begins.

"But I've never been to Afghanistan before and many people here don't even have enough bread to eat," Nazia sighs as she heads, two of her children in tow, toward registration counters festooned with white and black Taliban flags.

Nearly her entire family, eight sisters and their offspring, were deported to Afghanistan this year from Pakistan or Iran.

They are part of the biggest cross-border movement of people anywhere in the world.

Millions of Afghans have fled across the borders to Pakistan and Iran for decades – seeking refuge or employment - and the number escaping Afghanistan has continued to rise since the Taliban takeover in August 2021.

Most are now being forced to return as these two neighbours crack down on undocumented migrants. Nazia and her family were undocumented but the UN and human rights groups say the security sweep is reaching far beyond that group to include registered Afghans too. Even Pakistan now publicly says that Afghans with Proof of Registration cards are not exempt.

The expulsions show no sign of stopping.

The number forced to return this year from Pakistan and Iran has already reached another million, according to the UN's Refugee Agency, the UNHCR.

"In a little under three years, we've seen six million people, a population that is itself the size of a small country, come back to Afghanistan," observes Charlie Goodlake, spokesperson for the UNHCR in Afghanistan.

"We've never seen in recent history a return movement on this scale," he underlines, standing in the baking heat in the tented village close to the border.

It's a desolate landscape of tarpaulin and plastic shelters, many now tattered and torn, erected by the UN and other aid agencies to provide refuge for a few nights for a people arriving with nowhere to go.

Many returnees have not set foot in Afghanistan for decades; many like Nazia have never been here at all.

"I left 45 years ago during the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan and most of my brothers were born in Pakistan," explains Sarwar, who arrived a few days earlier with seven brothers and their families in a convoy of 40 people and the jumble of their worldly goods packed into a lumbering Pakistani lorry.

"We spent a long time there, so of course I felt heartbroken when they forced us out of our home," he says.

"But, despite all that pain, I am also happy because I am finally free of harassment by Pakistan's police."

Every family we met told us they had experienced prejudice and harassment by authorities in Pakistan.

The Pakistan government has not responded to the BBC's questions, but a foreign ministry spokesman told a briefing in Islamabad on Sunday that "the Government of Pakistan undertakes the necessary measures to prevent any instance of harassment or maltreatment of Afghan nationals in Pakistan. If such incidents have taken place, they are sporadic and are dealt with fully in accordance with the law".

Both Pakistan and Iran say it's past time for Afghans to go home, accusing some of posing a security risk, and others of being a financial burden.

The expulsions from Pakistan and alleged abuse intensified after a major escalation in fighting between Pakistan and Afghanistan last October. In February, Human Rights Watch highlighted "door-to-door raids, late-night home searches and arrests without warrants".

In Iran, which claimed last year to host more than four million undocumented Afghans, the mass deportations were accelerated after its 12-day war with Israel and the US in June 2025.

The New York based Centre for Human Rights in Iran accused the authorities of using the post-war climate to "cast suspicion on Afghan migrants - accusing them of espionage and branding them as potential spies for Israel".

The UN's refugee agency continues to underscore the humanitarian principle that any return should be "voluntary, safe and dignified".

But in Torkham, Sarwar's sister-in-law Zarina laments the precarious future they face: "We have no resources to start a business or earn a living, and we don't even own a tent to live in".

Inside the barren transit tent, which provides little escape from scorching 41C heat, Zarina sits alongside an anxious huddle of women and their children.

Are they worried about the future for women and girls in a country where the Taliban has barred women from much of public life, including secondary school and university?

Forty-year-old Zarina turns to make a sweeping gesture with her arm: "Look at them, they're all girls. Of course I'm worried."

Some returnees are not just worried; they're terrified.

"I don't leave this house," a former Afghan security guard, first deported from Iran and then Pakistan, nervously tells us when we meet him far from the border in what he hopes is a safe house.

"We are all living in fear including my wife and children who are also afraid to go outside."

He dismisses the Taliban government's amnesty, announced days after their return to power which declared that former government officials, security personnel and civil servants would not face retaliation and were encouraged to return to work.

"I have no trust in their amnesty because many of my colleagues have been killed." He says his case had been registered with the UN but was deported before he could be transferred to a safer country.

Financial hardship magnifies the pain. The steep cuts in foreign aid worldwide are especially sharp in Afghanistan where the Taliban are still stuck in sanctions linked to terrorism and human rights.

Pakistan confirmed on Sunday that 16,000 vulnerable Afghans have now been granted, on humanitarian grounds, a temporary exemption from being deported – a decision welcomed by the UN.

But sources estimate that the number of Afghans in Pakistan at risk of serious harm, including women and girls who would be denied education, could be as high as 250,000.

At the graceful foreign ministry compound in Kabul, Taliban Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi tries to put on a brave face.

"There's no doubt that we need some help," he admits. "There is pressure due to their return but in the long run, it will benefit them as well as Afghanistan."

In the first years after the Taliban swept to power in 2021, some of their ministers made light of humanitarian issues, saying God would provide.

The UN now estimates that 21.9 million people, nearly half the country, need assistance this year to survive. The UN's children agency, UNICEF, said last week that one million children faced "life-threatening" malnutrition.

"No country in the world could handle this kind of crisis on its own," UNHCR spokesperson Goodlake assesses, while acknowledging Taliban government efforts to help returnees as they arrive.

But, he adds, "We also know that many of the restrictions and edicts they put in place, particularly on women and girls, don't help us elicit international support".

Muttaqi reiterates his government's line that matters like girl's education are "internal issues" for Afghans to resolve.

The severe restrictions on the lives of girls and women is one of the major issues in the Taliban's international relationships and that has cost them. Five years on, only one country, Russia, has formally recognised their rule.

But when asked about this, Muttaqi points to the deepening diplomatic and economic ties with neighbours such as China and India, as well as Central Asian states.

As for Kabul's relative isolation from western nations, he asks, "those who didn't have relationships with us over the past five years, what have they achieved?"

He answers his own question: "Nothing."

We heard that word - "nothing" - from every family we met at Zero Point, but in a much different sense.

All were embarking on the hardest of homecomings, beginning all over again - with almost nothing.

Five years after the Taliban swept to power, does the West have any influence?

title: Inside the dangerous US mission that cleared Iran’s mines from Hormuz shipping lanes
description: CENTCOM's Adm. Brad Cooper details how Navy divers, SEALs and air power quietly cleared Iranian sea mines from the Strait of Hormuz shipping lanes.
fullText:
President Donald Trump declared last week that the United States had removed or detonated all mines in international waters in the Strait of Hormuz.

Now, the commander of U.S. Central Command has offered the clearest public account yet of the high-stakes operation behind that declaration: a monthslong effort in which U.S. forces quietly cleared Iranian sea mines from established international shipping lanes used by commercial vessels.

Other threats still stand between the cleared lanes and a return to normal activity in one of the world's most important waterways. The latest maritime guidance still classifies the Strait at a "SEVERE" threat level. Recent attacks have struck tankers near Oman, and oil flows remain far below prewar levels.

"We have successfully cleared sea mines in the Strait's international shipping lanes that were laid months ago by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps," CENTCOM Commander Adm. Brad Cooper said in a video update.

Trump Says Iran's Navy 'Obliterated' As Us Enforces Hormuz Blockade — But Key Threat Remains

"Internationally recognized transit routes in the Strait are free of Iranian sea mines thanks to the incredible work of the U.S. military," Cooper said.

Cooper identified the cleared area as the Strait's Traffic Separation Scheme, the long-standing system of opposing lanes that guides commercial vessels through the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman.

"Our forces meticulously and quietly cleared them of sea mine threats using a combination of Navy divers, Navy SEALs and U.S. air power from the Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps," Cooper said.

The operation was carried out as the Navy was in the middle of a major transition in how it handles mine warfare.

The service had retired its four Bahrain-based mine countermeasure ships the previous year as newer unmanned systems were still being fielded. In April, defense analyst Bryan Clark told Fox News Digital the Navy was at a "nadir" in its mine-sweeping capacity.

At the time, retired Vice Adm. Kevin Donegan, who previously commanded the Navy's 5th Fleet, said newer technology was increasingly being used to locate and neutralize mines, including unmanned systems that map the seabed and identify potential threats before explosive ordnance teams move in.

Cooper's account now shows U.S. forces relied on a broader combination of Navy divers, SEALs and air power to clear the international shipping lanes. CENTCOM has not disclosed the precise role each capability played.

"The circumstances were challenging and dangerous to say the least, but we got the job done," Cooper said. "Bottom line, today, international shipping lanes are open and momentum is building."

Donegan, who was not involved in the current operation, said mine-clearance operations begin with surface and subsurface vessels, including unmanned systems, locating and identifying possible mines. Once mines are identified, autonomous systems, specially trained Navy divers and SEALs can destroy or neutralize them.

Different sections of a waterway can be at different stages of the process at the same time, Donegan said, with forces neutralizing mines in one area while detection and identification continue elsewhere.

Throughout the operation, the Navy continues scanning the waterway to ensure it has not missed any mines, he said.

Donegan said the Navy uses a sophisticated detection model before declaring a waterway clear.

"In simplest terms, they have to conduct enough sweeps of the lanes to drive the probability of detection of mines to virtually 100% in the model," he said.

Donegan said the calculation takes into account factors including the detection systems and their effectiveness, characteristics of the waterway and the type of seabed.

White House Silent On Iran-oman Hormuz Plan Tehran Says Would Ban Us Warships

The Navy has also spent years preparing for such an operation. Donegan said elements of large-scale mine clearance in the Strait have been practiced through recurring NAVCENT mine-countermeasure exercises dating to 2012, along with regular Navy training.

Cooper said U.S. forces have assisted nearly 1,500 commercial vessels through the Strait in recent months by providing coordinated protection. Those ships carried nearly 750 million barrels of crude oil bound for global energy markets, he said.

The CENTCOM commander said the military is pursuing two missions at once: enforcing a naval blockade on Iran and protecting commercial passage through the Strait. He said that since the blockade resumed in mid-July, U.S. forces have turned around 75 vessels attempting to run it and disabled three that failed to comply with directions.

Cooper did not say how many mines U.S. forces found or destroyed.

Axios reported Thursday, citing U.S. officials, that American forces swept more than 200 mine-like objects from the main shipping lane. Of those objects, 11 were actual mines, and only a few had been properly deployed.

The figures illustrate the painstaking identification process Donegan described: Forces must investigate possible threats before determining which objects are actually mines.

CENTCOM has not provided further details on the systems used during the operation or how individual mines were neutralized. A defense official told Fox News Digital that the military would not discuss operational specifics for security reasons.

The broader maritime-security picture has yet to catch up with CENTCOM's declaration.

The latest Joint Maritime Information Center advisory, issued through the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations office on Aug. 25, keeps the Strait of Hormuz at a "SEVERE" threat level and says deliberate hostile action remains highly likely.

The advisory says mine-danger areas remain active and warns of a continued risk from drifting or uncharted mines in and near the Traffic Separation Scheme. It says clearance and mine-surveying operations continue throughout the Strait and that commercial traffic is expected to remain below prewar levels.

The assessment predates Cooper's video update. No public advisory downgrading the threat level or lifting the underlying warnings had been issued as of Friday.

Donegan said the possibility of drifting mines does not disappear entirely after a route has been cleared.

"In the Gulf there is always the danger of drifting mines that are not fixed, that are left over from this conflict or previous ones in the region," Donegan said. "That threat from those in the Gulf has historically been very low, especially due to currents in that area that make it unlikely that drifting mines stay in the lane and contact a commercial vessel."

Commercial crews are also still confronting attacks.

UKMTO reported that tankers near Oman were struck by unknown projectiles on Aug. 24 and Aug. 25, setting off fires that crews later extinguished. All crew members were reported safe in both incidents. The public alerts did not identify the vessels or attribute the strikes.

Oil flows through the Strait stood at about 5 million barrels per day Monday, down from more than 20 million before the war, according to Reuters, which cited provisional Vortexa tracking data.

The recovery remains uneven. Reuters reported Friday that seven commodity vessels transited the Strait on Thursday, down from 17 the day before and below the 10-day average of 15 vessels, based on preliminary shipping data.

Iran and Oman separately announced this week that they were discussing a temporary joint navigation corridor and a joint mine-clearance project. Their statements did not specify whether that work would cover the same Traffic Separation Scheme CENTCOM says U.S. forces have cleared.

Cooper's announcement provides the most detailed official account yet of the operation behind Trump's declaration and marks a significant step toward restoring commercial passage through the Strait.

The U.S. military says the recognized commercial lanes are open and protected. But the latest maritime risk guidance, continued attacks and sharply reduced traffic show that the broader Strait remains dangerous and disrupted.
